title: reportdoc hides every line indented four spaces or by a tab as code, so a list item's deep continuation or a 4-space sub-bullet never reaches a section reader
summary: visibleLinesIdx (go/internal/reportdoc/reportdoc.go:422) drops any line for which isIndentedCode (:473) holds, a leading tab or four spaces, whatever precedes it. CommonMark says an indented code block cannot interrupt a paragraph, and that a list item's content is indented to its content column, so a Changed Areas bullet wrapped as ``- `a.go` —`` then `    splits checkAll…` loses its explanation before changedAreaItems sees it, and the build floor still asks for a what/why. The Changed Areas list-item fix (2026-09-30) covers continuations indented fewer than four spaces and documents the limit in docs/architecture/build-explanation-contract.md; builders do write 4-space continuations (an accepted auditledger build explanation has three). visibleLinesIdx is the one fence/comment state machine every report validator shares, including verdict parsing, where hiding an indented example is deliberate, so the fix is its own component with its own review, not a change inside the explanation reader (architecture review of the list-item fix, HIGH-4).
fix: Treat an indented line as a paragraph or list-item continuation when the previous visible line is non-blank text (CommonMark: indented code cannot interrupt a paragraph), keeping a line after a blank line or a fence as code; prove no report validator's verdict or section parsing changes on the checked-in report corpus.
acceptance: A Changed Areas bullet whose explanation continues on a 4-space-indented line passes validateDocument (red today)
An indented block after a blank line is still hidden as code, and every existing reportdoc and verdict-parsing test stays green
The contract's 'indented fewer than four spaces' limit is removed in the same change
source: console, 2026-09-30 architecture review of the Changed Areas list-item fix (HIGH-4)
